market_summary: US tech stocks tumbled on November 2-3, 2026 amid disappointing earnings and AI spending concerns. Apple reported better-than-expected Q4 revenue at $114.5B but disappointed with weak gross margin guidance of 45-46%, down from current 47.9%, causing shares to fall 4% in premarket trading. Amazon missed earnings expectations with $1.89 EPS versus $2.01 consensus, and the Nasdaq fell 2.9% in its worst day since June. Meanwhile, Singapore's benchmark STI fell 1.4% in October with all three major banks (DBS, OCBC, UOB) scheduled to report Q3 results in early November, facing headwinds from bond-yield-driven mark-to-market losses and higher funding costs.

items.headline: Apple Q4 earnings beat on revenue but margin forecast disappoints, stock slides 4%
items.summary: <cite index="4-5,4-6">Apple posted Q4 EPS of $2.10 (vs $1.99 consensus) and revenue of $114.48B (vs $113.39B), both beating estimates.</cite> <cite index="6-7">However, gross margin guidance of 45-46% trailed the 46.3% consensus estimate.</cite>

items.headline: Amazon Q3 2026 earnings miss as revenue and EPS fall short of consensus
items.summary: <cite index="19-6,19-7">Amazon reported Q3 2026 EPS of $1.89 (miss vs $2.01 consensus) and revenue of $201.94B (miss vs estimate), with shares falling 1.4%.</cite>

items.headline: Microsoft earnings beat with strong AI revenue; analysts reward lower-than-expected AI spending discipline
items.summary: <cite index="15-2,15-3,15-7">Microsoft beat on top and bottom lines with healthy quarterly guidance and more strength from Azure, citing a $3.2 billion gain from its Anthropic stake and lower-than-expected costs from voluntary retirement programs.</cite>

items.headline: Nvidia Q2 FY2027 revenue hits $96.2B, up 106% year-on-year; next earnings November 17
items.summary: <cite index="42-2">Nvidia reported revenue for Q2 ended July 26, 2026, of $96.2 billion, up 18% from previous quarter and up 106% from a year ago.</cite> <cite index="43-1,43-2">Next earnings estimated for November 17, 2026.</cite>

items.headline: S&P 500 and Nasdaq tumble amid tech sell-off and AI spending concerns; Nasdaq posts worst day in nearly 5 months
items.summary: <cite index="19-2,19-4">US stocks ended sharply lower with the Nasdaq suffering its worst single-day percentage drop in nearly 5 months, tumbling 2.9% or 747.73 points to 25,437, as investors dumped AI stocks.</cite>

items.headline: DBS Group to report Q3 2026 earnings November 5; faces mark-to-market losses from bond yield surge
items.summary: <cite index="36-4,36-11,36-12">DBS reports November 5 with expected 3Q26 net profit SGD2.9bn-3.0bn vs SGD3.1bn in 2Q26 and income SGD6.0bn-6.1bn.</cite> <cite index="34-3">DBS faces pressure from bond-yield-driven mark-to-market losses.</cite>

items.headline: OCBC to report Q3 2026 earnings November 6; expected weaker profit on lower trading income
items.summary: <cite index="36-4,36-15,36-16">OCBC reports November 6 with expected 3Q26 net profit SGD1.9bn-2.0bn vs SGD2.2bn in 2Q26 and income SGD3.8bn-3.9bn.</cite> <cite index="36-6">Earnings expected marginally weaker sequentially on lower trading income.</cite>

items.headline: UOB to report Q3 2026 earnings November 4; least exposed to mark-to-market losses from bond yield surge
items.summary: <cite index="36-4">UOB reports November 4.</cite> <cite index="34-4,34-5">UOB is least exposed to mark-to-market losses given its small SGD7bn trading book, with estimated SGD50-80m q/q negative impact.</cite>

items.headline: Singapore STI's total returns slide 5.2% in October; tech index plunges 17.3%
items.summary: <cite index="32-6,32-7">The three major banks (DBS, OCBC, UOB) account for more than half of Singapore's benchmark index, and combined have shed more than $26 billion in market value over the past two trading sessions.</cite>

items.headline: Singapore bank shares tumble as JPMorgan warns surging bond yields threaten Q3 earnings
items.summary: <cite index="30-1,30-3">JPMorgan warned that surging long bond yields will hurt third-quarter earnings for Southeast Asian lenders, with DBS and OCBC falling more than 4% each and UOB dropping 5.2%.</cite>
